findings.title: Sidebar muted text (--sb-text-3) fails WCAG 1.4.3 contrast on every authenticated page (2.4:1)
findings.cvss: Not a CVSS-scored vulnerability. Risk rationale: this single token drives 3 of the 68 color-contrast instances on ALL 9 authenticated pages (the sidebar version sub-line plus two collapsible group labels), so it is the most pervasive defect. WCAG 2.1 Level AA conformance (1.4.3) is a contractual/regulatory requirement for Saudi public-sector and banking GRC procurement; a 2.4:1 ratio is barely over half the 4.5:1 floor and renders the version banner and risk/administration group headers effectively unreadable for low-vision users. High because it is global, repeated, and a named AA failure, but not Critical because it affects secondary/navigational chrome rather than primary task content.
findings.description: The dark sidebar uses the design token --sb-text-3 (#4A5C58) for its muted captions: the version/locale sub-line (“الإصدار ٢٫٠ · الرياض”) and the collapsible navigation group headers (إدارة المخاطر / الإدارة). On the sidebar background --sb-bg (#0B1F22) this yields a measured contrast ratio of 2.4:1, well below the WCAG 2.1 AA minimum of 4.5:1 for normal-size text. Because the sidebar is part of the global app shell injected on every route, axe flags these same 3 nodes on all 9 authenticated pages (login has no shell, hence 0 violations).
findings.rootCause: Token --sb-text-3 was chosen for visual subtlety against the very dark petrol sidebar without verifying contrast. At #4A5C58 on #0B1F22 it only reaches 2.4:1. The sibling token --sb-text-2 (#7E928F) already measures 5.19:1 on the same background and passes AA — the wrong (darker) tier of the two muted greys was assigned to these labels.
findings.evidence: audit/artifacts/e2e/results/axe/dashboard.json nodes[0..2]: fgColor #4a5c58, bgColor #0b1f22, contrastRatio 2.4, expectedContrastRatio 4.5:1 (font 10px normal for .sb-sub; 9px bold for the two group labels). Identical 3-node block appears in every per-page file (risk-register, dashboard, compliance, cyber, privacy, tprm, bcm, settings, knowledge-base). Recomputed locally with the WCAG relative-luminance formula: #4A5C58 on #0B1F22 = 2.40:1; proposed #9DB0AB = 7.49:1.
findings.impact: Low-vision users, users on low-quality/glare-affected displays, and users in bright ambient light cannot reliably read the product version, environment/region indicator, or the navigation group headers that organise the entire left-hand menu. This degrades wayfinding across the whole product and is a hard AA failure on every page.
findings.reproduction: 1. Run the live app (http://localhost:5173, backend :8084) and log in as admin/Admin@12345. 2. Open any authenticated route (e.g. /dashboard). 3. Run axe-core (the captured Playwright harness) → color-contrast violation with fgColor #4a5c58 / bgColor #0b1f22 / ratio 2.4 on .sb-sub and the two sb-group button spans. Artifact: audit/artifacts/e2e/results/axe/dashboard.json.
findings.resolution: Promote the sidebar muted captions to a contrast-checked tone. Re-define --sb-text-3 to a value that clears 4.5:1 on --sb-bg (#0B1F22). #9DB0AB (7.49:1) or #93A8A3 (6.79:1) both pass with comfortable margin while staying in the same desaturated teal-grey family. Apply the same change in the [data-theme="dark"] block (tokens.css:349) where --sb-text-3 is also #4A5C58 on an even darker #060F11 sidebar. After the change, re-run axe to confirm the 3 sidebar nodes drop on all 9 pages.

findings.title: Muted body/label grey (--ink-4) fails WCAG 1.4.3 on light surfaces (2.7:1)
findings.cvss: Not CVSS-scored. Risk rationale: --ink-4 (#8C9690) is referenced by dozens of component and page rules (text-dim, scale-seg-label, placeholders, empty-state captions, audit/capa/ethics/changes page labels) so although axe only caught it on /settings (3 of the 6 instances), the token is a latent AA failure anywhere it lands on a light surface. The team already documented and partially fixed this exact token for form placeholders (components.css:91, switched placeholders to --ink-3), which both proves the root cause and shows the fix is safe; remaining unconverted usages still fail. High due to breadth of usage on primary content labels.
locations: DOM selectors on /settings: .scale-seg-btn:nth-child(1)/(3)/(4) > .scale-seg-label (font-size labels صغير / كبير / كبير جدًا)
findings.description: The font-size segmented control on the Settings (تخصيص مساحة العمل) page renders its option labels (.scale-seg-label) in --ink-4 (#8C9690) over the segmented-control track surface --surface-2 (#F5F1E9). Measured contrast is 2.7:1 against the 4.5:1 AA floor. axe flagged 3 such labels on /settings. The same token is used for .text-dim and many secondary captions across components and page stylesheets, so this is a token-level defect, not a one-off.
findings.rootCause: --ink-4 (#8C9690) is the lightest 'still-text' ink in the ramp and was used for de-emphasised labels, but at #8C9690 it only reaches 2.71:1 on --surface-2 (#F5F1E9) and 2.88:1 on --surface (documented in components.css:91). The adjacent ramp tier --ink-3 (#5C6A65) reaches 5.03:1 on --surface-2 / 5.34:1 on --surface and passes AA — the same correction the team already applied to input placeholders (components.css:100, 136).
findings.evidence: audit/artifacts/e2e/results/axe/settings.json nodes[3..5]: fgColor #8c9690, bgColor #f5f1e9, contrastRatio 2.7, font 9.5px bold, expectedContrastRatio 4.5:1, target .scale-seg-btn ... > .scale-seg-label. Source comment components.css:91 already records “placeholder var(--ink-4) on var(--surface) = 2.88:1 → FAILS AA (4.5)”. Recomputed: #8C9690/#F5F1E9 = 2.71:1; #5C6A65/#F5F1E9 = 5.03:1.
findings.impact: Secondary labels, de-emphasised captions, empty-state text and the font-size picker labels are unreadable for low-vision users on light surfaces. Because --ink-4 is used widely, the real-world AA failure surface is larger than the 3 instances axe happened to catch on /settings.
findings.reproduction: 1. Log in (admin/Admin@12345), open /settings. 2. Run axe → color-contrast on .scale-seg-label spans, fgColor #8c9690 / bgColor #f5f1e9 / ratio 2.7. Artifact: audit/artifacts/e2e/results/axe/settings.json.
findings.resolution: Two-part fix. (a) For the specific failing control, change .scale-seg-label color from var(--ink-4) to var(--ink-3) (components.css:1935) — mirrors the documented placeholder fix. (b) Strategically, audit all var(--ink-4) text usages and migrate any that sit on light surfaces (--surface / --surface-2 / --surface-3) to var(--ink-3); reserve --ink-4 for non-text decoration (icons, borders, scrollbar thumb) where 1.4.3 does not apply. Optionally bump the --ink-4 token itself toward #6E7A75 (>=4.5:1 on --surface-2) if it must remain a text colour. Re-run axe on /settings to confirm.

findings.title: Risk score pills: white text on --risk-vhigh fails WCAG 1.4.3 (3.16:1) — 25 instances on the Risk Register
findings.cvss: Not CVSS-scored. Risk rationale: this is the single largest contributor — 25 of the 28 risk-register instances and 25 of the 68 total. The failing element is the residual/inherent risk SCORE PILL, primary decision-grade content in a risk-management tool. A user relying on these numerals to triage ‘very high’ risks is exactly the high-stakes path; an unreadable score in a GRC register is materially worse than chrome text, hence High.
locations: DOM: span.score-pill style="background: var(--risk-vhigh); color: rgb(255,255,255)" (values 12/15 etc.) on /risk
findings.description: On the Risk Register (/risk) the residual/inherent score pills render white (#FFFFFF) numerals on the --risk-vhigh fill (#D87560). Measured contrast is 3.16:1, below the 4.5:1 AA floor for normal text (the pill text is 11px bold, which is NOT 'large text' — large-text exemption requires >=18.66px bold / 24px). axe reported 25 identical instances on /risk, making this the dominant source of the page's 28 violations.
findings.rootCause: The --risk-vhigh heatmap tone (#D87560) is a mid-light terracotta tuned to look correct as a heatmap CELL fill, but it is too light to carry white text at small sizes: white-on-#D87560 = 3.16:1. The .score-pill component pairs that same fill with hard-coded white text, inheriting the failure. The heatmap-cell variant correctly uses dark text, but the pill does not.
findings.evidence: audit/artifacts/e2e/results/axe/risk-register.json: 25 nodes with fgColor #ffffff, bgColor #d87560, contrastRatio 3.16, font 11px bold, expectedContrastRatio 4.5:1; html ‘12’. axe-summary.json shows risk-register color-contrast(28). Recomputed: #FFFFFF/#D87560 = 3.17:1; white on a darkened #B5453A = 5.42:1; dark ink #15201D on #D87560 = 5.28:1.
findings.impact: Numeric risk scores — the most decision-critical content in the register — are below AA contrast for 25 cells. Low-vision risk managers may misread or fail to read scores, undermining the core triage function of the module.
findings.reproduction: 1. Log in, open /risk. 2. Run axe → 25 color-contrast violations, fgColor #ffffff / bgColor #d87560 / ratio 3.16 on span.score-pill. Artifact: audit/artifacts/e2e/results/axe/risk-register.json.
findings.resolution: Two viable fixes; prefer (a) to preserve the heatmap hue. (a) Switch .score-pill on the very-high tone to dark ink (color: var(--ink-1) #15201D) instead of white → 5.28:1; gate via a modifier class so only the light tones (med/high/vhigh) get dark ink while crit/danger keep white. (b) Introduce a dedicated, darker pill-fill token --risk-vhigh-strong (e.g. #B5453A, white text = 5.42:1) used only for .score-pill, leaving --risk-vhigh unchanged for heatmap cells. Do NOT simply darken --risk-vhigh globally without re-checking heatmap-cell dark-text contrast. Re-run axe on /risk.

findings.title: Accent / warning numerals fall just under contrast on cream surfaces (--accent-700 ~3.9:1 rendered, --warning 2.58:1 large)
findings.cvss: Not CVSS-scored. Risk rationale: borderline failures (3.0–3.9:1) on KPI/progress numerals across dashboard, compliance, cyber, privacy, bcm. They are small in count (1–2 per page) and partly transition-render artifacts, but they are still flagged AA failures on data-bearing figures. Medium: real but marginal, and one variant (the 48px BCM number at 2.58:1) only needs the 3:1 large-text threshold which a token swap clears.
locations: DOM: progress-label spans color:var(--accent-700) on /dashboard,/compliance,/cyber,/privacy; bcm score number color:var(--warning,#c47e00) at 48px
findings.description: Two related accent/amber colours produce small under-contrast figures on the cream surface --surface (#FAF8F4). (1) Progress-percentage and KPI numerals coloured var(--accent-700): axe sampled fgColor #a07622 (the value mid-CSS-transition) at 3.87:1 on dashboard, compliance, cyber, privacy. (2) The BCM readiness hero number (48px/700) coloured var(--warning) #C8932A measured 2.58:1; because it is large text the applicable threshold is 3:1, which it still fails.
findings.rootCause: TWO contributing causes. (i) The global CSS transition rule (tokens.css:368, `html * { transition: color 180ms }`) means axe occasionally samples an INTERMEDIATE colour while text animates — the static --accent-700 (#876019) actually measures 5.33:1 on #FAF8F4 and PASSES, but the captured rendered value #a07622 was a transition frame at 3.87:1. (ii) Independently, --warning (#C8932A) is genuinely too light for text on cream (2.58:1) and was used directly for the 48px BCM figure instead of the readable --warning-fg (#876019, 5.33:1).
findings.evidence: dashboard.json / compliance.json: fgColor #a07622, bgColor #faf8f4, contrastRatio 3.87, 12px bold, target .progress-label span (color: var(--accent-700)). bcm.json node[3]: fgColor #c8932a, bgColor #faf8f4, contrastRatio 2.58, 48px bold, expectedContrastRatio 3:1, html color:var(--warning,#c47e00). Recomputed: static --accent-700 #876019/#FAF8F4 = 5.33:1 (passes); --warning #C8932A/#FAF8F4 = 2.58:1 (fails 3:1); --warning-fg #876019 = 5.33:1 (passes 3:1).
findings.impact: KPI and progress percentages, and the BCM readiness score, render at sub-AA contrast at least transiently, and the BCM large number persistently. Low-vision users may misread compliance/readiness figures. Lower-impact than A11Y-001..003 because counts are small and one cause is a transient animation frame.
findings.reproduction: 1. Log in, open /bcm → axe color-contrast on the 48px readiness number, fgColor #c8932a / ratio 2.58 (artifact bcm.json). 2. Open /dashboard or /compliance → color-contrast on .progress-label spans, rendered fgColor #a07622 / ratio 3.87 (artifacts dashboard.json, compliance.json).
findings.resolution: (a) For data figures, never use --warning/--accent-500 as a TEXT colour on light surfaces; use --warning-fg / --accent-700 (the dedicated readable foreground tones). Change the BCM hero number from color: var(--warning) to color: var(--warning-fg) (#876019, 5.33:1, clears the 3:1 large-text bar with margin). (b) To stop axe sampling transition frames AND to remove the marginal accent-700 failures, exclude `color` from the global transition on text, or shorten it: the audit color should be the settled value. Consider tightening --accent-700 to #73520F (6.73:1) for extra headroom so even a transition frame stays safe. Re-run axe on /bcm and /dashboard.

findings.title: Heatmap score numerals fail contrast on medium/high risk cells (3.0–3.4:1)
findings.cvss: Not CVSS-scored. Risk rationale: the 5×5 risk heatmap on /dashboard renders cell scores (10/15/16) in a tinted dark amber/terracotta that drops to 3.0–3.4:1 on the --risk-med / --risk-high fills. These are data-bearing numerals but redundant with cell position/colour, and the count is small (5 of dashboard's 10). Medium.
findings.description: The dashboard 5×5 risk heatmap renders the numeric score inside each cell (.heatmap-score). On the --risk-med fill (#F0D58A) the auto-derived dark text (#78714e) measures 3.41:1, and on --risk-high (#E8A878) the dark text (#745d46) measures 3.03:1 — both below the 4.5:1 AA floor for the 12px bold numerals. axe reported 5 such cells on /dashboard.
findings.rootCause: The heatmap-score text colour is a muted brown tuned to sit softly on the tint, but it does not reach AA against the lighter med/high fills. The fills themselves are correct heatmap tones; the score text simply needs a darker, higher-contrast ink rather than a hue-matched muted brown.
findings.evidence: audit/artifacts/e2e/results/axe/dashboard.json nodes for td[title="L2 × I5 = 10"] etc.: fgColor #78714e / bgColor #f0d58a / 3.41:1, and fgColor #745d46 / bgColor #e8a878 / 3.03:1, 12px bold, expectedContrastRatio 4.5:1. Recomputed with a high-contrast ink --ink-2 #2E3A36: on #F0D58A = 8.22:1, on #E8A878 = 5.81:1 (both pass AA).
findings.impact: The numeric scores overlaid on medium/high heatmap cells are below AA contrast. The information is partially redundant (cell colour + position convey severity), so impact is moderate, but the explicit numerals are still hard to read for low-vision users.
findings.reproduction: 1. Log in, open /dashboard. 2. Run axe → color-contrast on td.heatmap-cell > .heatmap-score for the med/high cells (fgColor #78714e/#745d46). Artifact: audit/artifacts/e2e/results/axe/dashboard.json.
findings.resolution: Set the .heatmap-score text colour to a fixed high-contrast dark ink (var(--ink-2) #2E3A36 or --ink-1) for the light tones (vlow/low/med/high) rather than a hue-matched brown. --ink-2 on #F0D58A = 8.22:1 and on #E8A878 = 5.81:1, both pass AA, and the same ink reads cleanly across all light heatmap fills. For the dark vhigh/crit fills keep white/light text. Re-run axe on /dashboard.

findings.title: Manual-only WCAG criteria not covered by automated axe scan — keyboard, focus, landmarks, motion (require manual verification)
findings.cvss: Not CVSS-scored. Risk rationale: automated tools detect only ~30–40% of WCAG issues. The captured axe run covers parseable rules (contrast, names, roles, landmarks-as-coded) but CANNOT assert keyboard operability, visible focus, logical focus order, meaningful sequence, or motion preferences — all AA/A criteria that must be verified by a human. Flagging as Medium because these are unverified, not confirmed failures; they represent audit coverage gaps that block a clean AA sign-off.
locations: Whole authenticated app shell (tss-grc-ui-v2): sidebar nav, collapsible groups (button[aria-controls="sb-group-*"]), modals/dialogs, data tables (.score-pill rows on /risk), segmented controls (.scale-seg-btn on /settings)
findings.description: axe-core verified that /login has 0 violations and that all 9 authenticated pages fail ONLY color-contrast (68 instances). However, axe cannot evaluate interaction- and structure-level success criteria. The following AA/A criteria are NOT covered by the captured artifacts and require manual testing before an AA conformance claim can be made: (a) 2.1.1 Keyboard — every control (sidebar toggles, modals, tables, segmented font-size control) operable without a mouse and no traps (2.1.2); (b) 2.4.7 Focus Visible — a clearly visible focus indicator on every focusable element; the design defines --focus-ring tokens (tokens.css:217) but their actual application must be verified per component; (c) 2.4.3 Focus Order — tab order matches the visual/RTL reading order (critical for an Arabic-primary RTL UI); (d) 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence and 1.3.1 Info & Relationships — DOM order and landmark/heading structure (the app injects a global shell into #app-shell; <aside class="sb"> exists but presence of <nav>/<main>/<header> landmarks and a logical heading hierarchy must be confirmed); (e) 2.3.1/2.3.3 motion — the global `html * { transition }` and any animations must honour prefers-reduced-motion.
findings.rootCause: Automated scanning has inherent coverage limits; the dynamic test harness ran axe (rule-based) and Lighthouse (which gave /login a11y = 100, also automated-only). No keyboard-walk, screen-reader pass, or reduced-motion check was captured. This is a methodology coverage gap, not a code defect — but it means AA conformance is currently unproven for the interaction/structure criteria.
findings.evidence: audit/artifacts/e2e/results/axe-summary.json shows every authenticated page has exactly 1 violation = color-contrast and login = 0; rules arrays contain ONLY 'color-contrast(n)'. No axe rule output exists for focus-order, keyboard, or motion (axe does not test these). Lighthouse a11y score for /login = 100 is likewise automated-only and does not assert keyboard/SR behaviour. The shell DOM (relatedNodes html '<aside class="sb">') confirms a sidebar exists but the artifacts do not capture landmark/role coverage for <main>/<nav>/<header>.
findings.impact: Without manual verification, the platform cannot claim WCAG 2.1 AA conformance even after the contrast fixes land. Keyboard-only and screen-reader users (a regulated requirement for Saudi government/banking procurement) may be blocked by issues invisible to axe — e.g. an unreachable modal, a missing focus ring, an RTL tab-order mismatch, or non-throttled motion.
findings.reproduction: Manual protocol (to be executed against http://localhost:5173, admin/Admin@12345): 1) Keyboard walk every page using only Tab/Shift+Tab/Enter/Space/Esc/arrows — confirm all controls reachable, no traps, sidebar group buttons (aria-controls) expand/collapse via keyboard. 2) Observe a visible focus indicator on each focusable element (verify --focus-ring renders). 3) Confirm tab order follows RTL visual order. 4) Run a screen reader (NVDA + Windows / VoiceOver) and verify landmarks (nav/main/header), heading order, and that aria-controls/aria-pressed states are announced. 5) Enable OS 'reduce motion' and confirm transitions/animations are suppressed.
findings.resolution: Commission a manual WCAG 2.1 AA pass covering SC 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 1.3.1, 1.3.2, 2.3.1, 2.3.3 and screen-reader smoke tests with NVDA + VoiceOver. Ensure the app shell wraps content in semantic landmarks (<nav> for .sb, <main> for content, <header> for the top bar), that --focus-ring is applied to all interactive elements (not just inputs), and that a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block neutralises the global transition (tokens.css:367 already guards the mode-switch transition behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference — verify ALL motion is similarly guarded). Track each criterion in the pass/fail matrix in A11Y-007.
references: WCAG 2.1 SC 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below (A)

findings.title: WCAG 2.1 AA conformance summary — per-criterion pass/fail view across the dynamic a11y audit
findings.cvss: Not CVSS-scored. Informational roll-up of the dynamic accessibility audit: 1 page clean (login), 9 pages failing AA on a single root rule (color-contrast, 68 instances) traced to 5 design tokens, plus manual criteria left unverified. Provided so reviewers see the AA picture at a glance and can sign off criterion-by-criterion once fixes + manual pass land.
findings.description:
PER-CRITERION AA/A PASS/FAIL VIEW (dynamic scan + analysis):

| WCAG SC | Level | Status | Evidence / Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) | AA | FAIL | 68 instances across 9 authenticated pages; 0 on /login. Root cause = 5 tokens: --sb-text-3 (2.4:1, A11Y-001), --ink-4 (2.7:1, A11Y-002), --risk-vhigh white pills (3.16:1, A11Y-003), --accent-700/--warning (2.58–3.87:1, A11Y-004), heatmap score ink (3.0–3.4:1, A11Y-005). |
| 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast | AA | PARTIAL/REVIEW | axe flagged the 48px BCM number under the 3:1 large/non-text threshold (A11Y-004); verify UI-component & graphical-object contrast manually. |
| 1.4.1 Use of Color | A | NOT TESTED (manual) | Risk severity conveyed by colour pills/heatmap — confirm a non-colour cue (the numeric score) is always present. |
| 1.1.1 Non-text Content | A | PASS (automated) | No image-alt / aria-name violations reported by axe on any page. |
| 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value | A | PASS (automated) | No axe violations; buttons expose aria-controls/aria-pressed (seen in DOM). Manual SR confirmation still advised. |
| 1.3.1 Info & Relationships | A | NOT TESTED (manual) | Landmark/heading structure not asserted by artifacts — A11Y-006. |
| 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence | A | NOT TESTED (manual) | RTL DOM/reading-order — A11Y-006. |
| 2.1.1 Keyboard / 2.1.2 No Trap | A | NOT TESTED (manual) | A11Y-006. |
| 2.4.3 Focus Order | A | NOT TESTED (manual) | A11Y-006. |
| 2.4.7 Focus Visible | AA | NOT TESTED (manual) | --focus-ring tokens defined (tokens.css:217); per-component application unverified — A11Y-006. |
| 2.3.1 Three Flashes / 2.3.3 Animation | A/AAA | NOT TESTED (manual) | Global transition present; reduce-motion coverage to confirm — A11Y-006. |

NET: The only AUTOMATED-detectable AA failure is 1.4.3, and it is fully traced to design tokens with exact before/after values (A11Y-001..005). All remaining AA/A criteria are unverified pending the manual pass (A11Y-006). /login already passes the automated scan (0 violations, Lighthouse a11y = 100).
findings.rootCause: All 68 automated failures share ONE category (color-contrast / SC 1.4.3) and reduce to FIVE design tokens defined in tss-grc-ui-v2/src/styles/tokens.css. Fixing those tokens (per A11Y-001..005) clears the entire automated AA gap; the manual criteria (A11Y-006) are a separate coverage workstream.
findings.evidence: axe-summary.json: login violations=0; risk-register color-contrast(28), dashboard(10), compliance(6), settings(6), cyber(4), privacy(4), bcm(4), tprm(3), knowledge-base(3) = 68 total, every byImpact = {serious:1}, every rules entry = color-contrast only. Per-page files confirm the distinct fg/bg pairs: #4a5c58/#0b1f22 (2.4), #8c9690/#f5f1e9 (2.7), #ffffff/#d87560 (3.16), #a07622/#faf8f4 (3.87), #c8932a/#faf8f4 (2.58), #78714e/#f0d58a (3.41), #745d46/#e8a878 (3.03). Lighthouse a11y /login = 100 (automated).
findings.impact: Gives auditors and the dev team a single criterion-level scoreboard: one AA rule fails automatically (fixable via 5 token edits), several criteria remain unproven and need a manual pass before an AA conformance statement is defensible for Saudi public-sector / banking procurement.
findings.reproduction: Re-run the captured Playwright + axe-core harness against all 10 routes and Lighthouse against /login; compare against audit/artifacts/e2e/results/axe-summary.json. After applying A11Y-001..005, expect color-contrast(n) to drop to 0 on all pages; then execute the A11Y-006 manual protocol to close the remaining criteria.
findings.resolution: 1) Land token fixes A11Y-001..005 (effort S–M each) and re-run axe to confirm 1.4.3 reaches 0 violations on all 9 pages. 2) Execute the A11Y-006 manual protocol (keyboard, focus, landmarks, SR, motion) and record each criterion as Pass/Fail in this matrix. 3) Only after both are green may an AA conformance claim (e.g. a VPAT/ACR) be issued. Keep /login as the regression baseline (0 violations).
findings.patchBefore:
Automated AA status BEFORE fixes:
  1.4.3 Contrast = FAIL (68 instances / 9 pages)
  All other AA/A criteria = unverified (manual)
findings.patchAfter:
Target AA status AFTER fixes + manual pass:
  1.4.3 Contrast = PASS (0 axe violations, all tokens >= 4.5:1 / 3:1)
  2.1.1, 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 1.3.1, 1.3.2, 2.3.x = verified PASS via manual protocol
references: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.1 Use of Color (Level A)
